desc: Immaculate Constellation is the name of an alleged unacknowledged special access program that entered the public record in October 2024 through the journalist Michael Shellenberger and entered the Congressional Record on 13 November 2024. Shellenberger, founder of Public, reported that a current or former US government official acting as a UAP whistleblower had provided him a report; the source told Public the programme is 'a strategic intelligence program', and a former intelligence community official subsequently confirmed its existence to him. Shellenberger's written testimony to the House Oversight Committee states the whistleblower alleges the Department of Defense created the programme in 2017 after the New York Times published on AATIP, and that a source subsequently told him it 'is controlled by the White House and executed and administrated by the DOD to avoid compliance with Title 10' - which is a specific, testable allegation about the legal mechanism of concealment, not a vague assertion of secrecy. The twelve-page document has two sections: the first describing the USAP, the second concerning US Government imagery intelligence. Under oath Shellenberger characterised Immaculate Constellation as serving 'as a central or parent USAP that consolidates observations of UAPs by both tasked and untasked collection platforms', holding 'high-quality imagery intelligence and measurement and signature intelligence' drawn from low Earth orbit, the upper atmosphere, aviation altitudes and maritime environments, across infrared, forward-looking infrared, full motion video and still photography. The report catalogues recurring morphologies observed from 1991 to 2022 - spheres and orbs, discs and saucers, ovals and tic-tacs, triangles, boomerang and arrowhead forms, and irregular or organic shapes - and describes specific incidents: 'orbs surrounding and forcing an F-22 out of its patrol area'; 'the crew of a Navy aircraft carrier watched a small orange/red sphere rapidly descend from a high altitude of 100 to 200 yards directly above the flight deck'; and 'a roughly 13-minute long, high-definition, full-color video of a white orb UAP coming out of the ocean approximately 20 miles off the coast of Kuwait ... joined by another orb that briefly comes into the frame from the left.' Under questioning from Rep. Clay Higgins, Shellenberger confirmed 'I do' know the author, and refused to place his sources: 'I will not say ... I protect my sources, and I am not willing to reduce the potential universe of where my sources might be.' Chairwoman Nancy Mace then moved the document into the record: 'Committee staff asked me to go ahead, and I will do it, to enter into the Congressional Record this 12-page document that Michael Shellenberger brought today that describes the Immaculate Constellation government program.' It appears in the hearing's Index of Documents as 'Report, Pentagon, Immaculate Constellation; submitted by Rep. Mace.' The official response is the important part of this dossier. The Department of Defense says it has no record of such a programme; Pentagon spokesperson Sue Gough has stated the Department has 'no record'; former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick has denied it exists. No AARO product has ever addressed it: not the FY2024 annual report, not the FY2025 report delivered 21 July 2026, not any statement for the record, and no PURSUE tranche between 8 May and 7 August 2026 released anything under the name. In 2025 a self-identified whistleblower said he had located the material in a folder labelled '2018 Schriever Wargame', and Jason Colavito assessed that the claimant had mistaken fictitious wargame documents for secret UFO revelations - an assessment that, whatever its merits, addresses a later claimant's provenance story and not Shellenberger's source. The board's position is that the load-bearing fact is procedural: a named programme is in the Congressional Record, the Department's answer is a records assertion rather than a denial of existence, and in the twenty-one months since no office has produced a written response, a records search declaration, or a classification review.

claims.text: Shellenberger's written testimony states: 'these individuals have revealed the name of an active and highly secretive DOD "Unacknowledged Special Access Program," or USAP. The source of the document told Public that the USAP is a "strategic intelligence program" that is part of the US military's family of long-standing, highly-sensitive programs dealing with various aspects of the UAP "problem."'

The whistleblower's report, as quoted in the written testimony, says 'the Executive Branch has been managing UAP/NHI issues without Congressional knowledge, oversight, or authorization for some time, quite possibly decades.'

The written testimony states: 'The whistleblower alleges that the DOD created the USAP, called "Immaculate Constellation," in 2017 after the New York Times published an article describing an informal Pentagon UAP program called "Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program," or AATIP.'

The written testimony states: 'After publication, a source told me that the SAP is controlled by the White House and executed and administrated by the DOD to avoid compliance with Title 10 of the United States Code. "It is essentially a DOD Program," the person said, "as the White House directed the SECDEF to run it. But that's the loophole."'

The written testimony identifies the notification statutes that should apply: '10 USC Sec 119 and 50 USC Sec 3093 are applicable here. DEPSECDEF must notify congress regarding DOD SAPs and the President must notify regarding Covert Action. For UAPs this is apparently not happening because the White House has a loophole for non-covert action waived programs.'

The report says 'IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION serves as a central or "parent" USAP that consolidates observations' of UAPs 'by both tasked and untasked collection platforms', and 'includes high-quality Imagery Intelligence (IMINT) and Measurement and Signature Intelligence (MASINT) of UAPs' from collection 'positioned in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the upper atmosphere' and at aviation and maritime altitudes.

The report describes an incident in which 'The F-22 broke trajectory and attempted to evade but was intercepted and boxed in by approximately 3-6 UAPs', with one UAP maintaining 'a rigid spatial relationship with the F-22, maintaining its exact position and orientation parallel with the F-22's cockpit despite multiple evasive rolls and maneuvers', after which 'the F-22 was forced out of the mission area under the escort of the UAP formation.'

The written testimony records a source warning that 'simply printing the name "Immaculate Constellation" could trigger government surveillance of me under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) of whoever publishes it. "They won't comment on it, but talking about it will put you in the danger zone," I was told.'
Department of Defense spokesperson Sue Gough is quoted in the written testimony: 'The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called "IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION."'

From the dais on 13 November 2024, Rep. Nancy Mace described the document as '12 pages about this unacknowledged special access program that your government says does not exist', and reported that 'Representative Luna just told me, if I say, "Immaculate Constellation," I will be on some list. Maybe a FISA warrant. So, come at me bro, I guess.'
Asked by Rep. Mace what the programme's mission is and how it is funded, Shellenberger answered under oath: 'it is an unacknowledged special access program. Its mission is to document UAPs.'

Asked by Rep. Clay Higgins whether he knew the report's author, Shellenberger answered 'I do'; asked what the author's sources were, he answered that they are 'described in the report - these data bases, the Immaculate Constellation program'.

At the same hearing, retired Rear Adm. Tim Gallaudet testified: 'I concluded that the UAP information must have been classified within a special access program managed by an intelligence agency. That is, a compartmented program that even senior officials, including myself, were not read into.'

At the same hearing, asked by Rep. Mace 'Are you read into secret UAP crash retrieval programs?', Luis Elizondo answered: 'We would have to have a conversation in a closed session, ma'am. I signed documentation 3 years ago that restricts my ability to discuss specifically crash retrievals.'

dossier.denialPosture: Department of Defense spokesperson Sue Gough is quoted in Shellenberger's written testimony as saying: 'The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called "IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION."' That is a records assertion rather than a denial of existence, and it is the standard formulation available to an office without read-on to an unacknowledged compartment. Rep. Mace characterised it from the dais as a programme 'that your government says does not exist'. No further departmental statement has been made in the twenty-one months since.
dossier.narrative:
In October 2024 Michael Shellenberger, founder of the outlet Public, reported that a current or former US government official acting as a UAP whistleblower had provided him a report naming an active and highly secretive Department of Defense unacknowledged special access program. On 13 November 2024 he appeared under oath before the House Oversight Committee and the twelve-page document was entered into the Congressional Record from the dais.

His written testimony sets out the constitutional frame before it names anything. It cites 10 U.S.C. 119 and 50 U.S.C. 3093 - the SAP notification statute and the covert action statute - and states: 'DEPSECDEF must notify congress regarding DOD SAPs and the President must notify regarding Covert Action. For UAPs this is apparently not happening because the White House has a loophole for non-covert action waived programs.' The whistleblower's own words, as quoted in the testimony, are that 'the Executive Branch has been managing UAP/NHI issues without Congressional knowledge, oversight, or authorization for some time, quite possibly decades.'

The source characterisation of the programme is that it 'is a "strategic intelligence program" that is part of the US military's family of long-standing, highly-sensitive programs dealing with various aspects of the UAP "problem."' The report itself, as quoted in the testimony, says 'IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION serves as a central or "parent" USAP that consolidates observations' of UAPs 'by both tasked and untasked collection platforms.' It 'includes high-quality Imagery Intelligence (IMINT) and Measurement and Signature Intelligence (MASINT) of UAPs', drawn from 'a blend of directed and incidental collection capabilities positioned in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the upper atmosphere' and at aviation and maritime altitudes. The most common shapes in the dataset are given as 'spheres/orbs, discs/saucers, ovals/tic-tacs, triangles, boomerang/arrowhead, and irregular/organic.'

The incident material is specific enough to be checkable by anyone with access to the underlying databases. One case: orbs surrounding and forcing an F-22 out of its patrol area, in which 'The F-22 broke trajectory and attempted to evade but was intercepted and boxed in by approximately 3-6 UAPs', with one UAP maintaining 'a rigid spatial relationship with the F-22, maintaining its exact position and orientation parallel with the F-22's cockpit despite multiple evasive rolls and maneuvers.' Another: the crew of a Navy aircraft carrier watching a 'small orange-red sphere' rapidly descend from high altitude to 100-200 yards directly above the flight deck. A third, sourced after publication: a roughly thirteen-minute high-definition full-colour video of a white orb emerging from the ocean approximately twenty miles off the coast of Kuwait, filmed from a helicopter, joined mid-video by a second orb, discovered by the source on SIPR.

The testimony also records a warning about the name itself. 'A source warned that simply printing the name "Immaculate Constellation" could trigger government surveillance of me under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) of whoever publishes it. "They won't comment on it, but talking about it will put you in the danger zone," I was told.' From the dais that day Rep. Nancy Mace said the same thing out loud: 'And Representative Luna just told me, if I say, "Immaculate Constellation," I will be on some list. Maybe a FISA warrant. So, come at me bro, I guess.'

The Department's response is a records assertion, and Shellenberger printed it in his own testimony: 'DOD spokesperson Sue Gough said, "The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called 'IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION.'"' That is not a statement that the programme does not exist. It is a statement about what a records search returned, made by a public affairs office that would not hold the read-on to an unacknowledged compartment. Mace's framing on the dais captured the structure exactly: '12 pages about this unacknowledged special access program that your government says does not exist.'

Two further items from the same hearing bear on the plausibility of the mechanism rather than the name. Retired Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet, formerly the Navy's chief meteorologist, testified: 'I concluded that the UAP information must have been classified within a special access program managed by an intelligence agency. That is, a compartmented program that even senior officials, including myself, were not read into.' And Luis Elizondo, asked directly by Mace whether he was read into secret UAP crash retrieval programmes, answered: 'We would have to have a conversation in a closed session, ma'am. I signed documentation 3 years ago that restricts my ability to discuss specifically crash retrievals.'

Under questioning from Rep. Clay Higgins, Shellenberger confirmed he knows the report's author - 'I do' - and declined to characterise the author's institutional position. Asked by Mace what the programme's mission is, he answered that it is an unacknowledged special access program whose 'mission is to document UAPs'. He also stated that when he checked the report against existing public cases he 'did not find it based on existing cases; it was new cases for me', which he offered as evidence against circular reporting.

What the record does not contain is any independent corroboration of the name from a second identified source, any document bearing the programme name, or any executive branch statement beyond the records denial. The name has never appeared in an AARO annual report, in any PURSUE tranche description, or in any published DoD product.
openQuestions: The identity and institutional position of the report's author, which Shellenberger confirmed he knows but declined to disclose.
Whether any congressional committee has formally requested a SAP notification search under 10 U.S.C. 119 against the alleged programme, and what the response was.
Whether the 'non-covert action waived program' loophole described in the testimony is a real category in current SAP practice, and which office administers such programmes.

Whether the specific incidents described - the F-22 boxing event, the CVN flight deck sphere, the Kuwait helicopter video on SIPR - correspond to identifiable case numbers in AARO, UAPTF or service databases.
No document bearing the programme name has ever been published; the only artefact in the public record is the twelve-page report entered by Rep. Mace.
Claims elsewhere that former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick denied the programme could not be verified against a primary source for this dossier and are not asserted here.
dossier.whatItIs: Immaculate Constellation is the name of an alleged unacknowledged special access program that entered public reporting in October 2024 through the journalist Michael Shellenberger and entered the Congressional Record on 13 November 2024. According to the whistleblower report Shellenberger delivered to the House Oversight Committee, it was created by the Department of Defense in 2017 after the New York Times published on AATIP, and functions as a central or parent USAP consolidating UAP observations from tasked and untasked collection platforms. The Department of Defense has stated it has no record of any such program.
dossier.whyImplicated: The allegation is not that a secret exists but that a specific legal mechanism was used to keep it from Congress. Shellenberger's sworn written testimony states that a source told him the SAP 'is controlled by the White House and executed and administrated by the DOD to avoid compliance with Title 10 of the United States Code', adding: 'It is essentially a DOD Program, as the White House directed the SECDEF to run it. But that's the loophole.' The same testimony identifies the statutes that should have compelled notification - 10 U.S.C. 119 and 50 U.S.C. 3093 - and asserts that the White House has a loophole for non-covert-action waived programs. That is a falsifiable structural claim about how a compartment can be run without triggering either SAP notification to the congressional defense committees or covert action findings to the intelligence committees. If true, it explains the entire pattern of this board: programmes that no oversight body can locate because no oversight body was ever the notification recipient.

entityInfo.desc: The shape of the official response matters more than its content. The Department of Defense has said it has 'no record' of the programme - a records assertion, and the standard formulation used by an office without read-on to an unacknowledged compartment. It has not said the programme does not exist. Former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick has denied it, but he departed AARO in December 2023, eleven months before the report surfaced. AARO itself has never addressed the name in any published product: not the FY2024 annual report, not the FY2025 report delivered 21 July 2026, not any statement for the record, and not in any of the five PURSUE tranches published between 8 May and 7 August 2026. AARO's own declassification information paper of September 2025 concedes that it cannot declassify independently and must request review from originating offices - which is a structural explanation for why an office chartered to resolve anomalies would have nothing to say about a compartment it is not read into. The result is that a named alleged USAP has sat in the Congressional Record for twenty-one months without a written executive branch response of any kind.
